subject: coro-code
title: Bash permission system removed at HEAD and left removed: requires_confirmation() returns false with the comment 'Bash commands can be dangerous'
evidence: commit 679c57af (HEAD, 2025-10-30) 'temporarily disable the access permission system for the bash tool'; cli/src/tools/bash.rs:466-467; no tool in tree returns true (core/src/tools/base.rs:25-27 default false); grep permission|sandbox|deny across cli+core finds no binding control; fail-closed confirmation seam in loop (core/src/agent/core.rs:449-453) is unreachable dead code
one_why: Worse default than nanocoder's opt-in jail (which at least exists) and than codel only by honesty: arbitrary shell as the user with zero gate, and the removal commit's 'temporarily' has stood ~11 months (remote pushed_at verified); the corpus's cleanest example of guardrail-stripping as a shipping default.

subject: coro-code
title: Auto-compaction threshold is computed against params.max_tokens (the completion budget, default 8192) instead of the model context window
evidence: core/src/agent/core.rs:72,204 (ConversationManager::new(llm_config.params.max_tokens.unwrap_or(8192))); core/src/agent/tokens/conversation_manager.rs:110-127 (usage_ratio = estimated context tokens / that limit, tiers at 0.7/0.8/0.9)
one_why: On a 128k-window model the agent enters heavy summarization at ~7.3k estimated context tokens -- permanent amnesia on any real task; a one-line config field (model context size) fixes a whole-lane design bug, and nobody upstream has fixed it in 11 months.

subject: coro-code
title: Three-tier compaction (tool-output truncation / LLM segment summary / recent-only) with tool-call-pair-preserving split points
one_why: The pair-aware cut point plus graduated light-before-heavy ordering is the right shape at ~700 LOC and is actually tested -- the concept is worth keeping even though coro's trigger binding is broken (finding coro-code-2).

subject: coro-code
title: --trajectory-file logs 'Trajectory saved to' but nothing is ever written; --must-patch writes a literal placeholder file
evidence: cli/src/commands/run.rs:57 (TrajectoryRecorder::new(), fileless), :94-96 (info! 'Trajectory saved to' with no save call; fileless recorder.rs:61 has auto_save=false), core/src/trajectory/recorder.rs:70 (with_file ctor never called), run.rs:85-90 (patch file content '# Changes would be recorded here')
one_why: Headless batch users get exit-0 success, a confident 'saved' log line, and no artifact -- the failure mode that silently destroys eval runs; a working with_file one-liner exists in-tree, it is simply not called.

subject: coro-code
title: CKG tool: tree-sitter-parsed code knowledge graph persisted in bundled-sqlite, shipped as one 796-LOC tool
evidence: cli/src/tools/ckg.rs:1-30 (tree-sitter grammars for 8 languages, rusqlite Connection), cli/Cargo.toml:63 (rusqlite bundled), registered at cli/src/tools/registry.rs via CkgToolFactory (cli/src/tools/mod.rs:12)
one_why: Only subject so far with a persistent structural code index as a first-party tool; unproven as retrieval (no tests, no loop integration evidence), so worth concept-level watching rather than copying -- unique in the corpus, mechanism depth unverified.

subject: coro-code
title: MockLlmClient drives compression tests so summarization paths are exercised without API keys
evidence: core/src/agent/tokens/conversation_manager.rs:630-668 (MockLlmClient returning canned summary), :672-712 (compression-applied / no-compression / usage-ratio cases); core/src/agent/core.rs:1017-1051 (mock client for agent construction)
one_why: Small but honest faux-provider coverage of the one token-economy component where live keys would make CI impossible; convergence with the seeded id -- coro's version is thin (no scripted tool-call sequences) so the loop itself stays untested.

subject: coro-code
title: MIT OR Apache-2.0 declared in Cargo.toml only; no LICENSE file anywhere in the tree
evidence: Cargo.toml:10 (license = 'MIT OR Apache-2.0'); find . -iname 'LICENSE*' excluding .git: no results; GitHub API license:null for Blushyes/coro-code; README.md badge links LICENSE-MIT which does not exist
one_why: An SPDX manifest string is not a grant of rights; until the texts land, all coro-code findings here are concept-only and effort_for_us assumes clean-room implementation -- convergence with manifest-only-license (g3, zap-coding-agent).
